newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols up in August options.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols up in August options.

text.p: Volatilities in major U.S. index options rose in August and other longer-dated series as the underlying market softened slightly after another record-setting day Wednesday, traders said.
"Volatility came in quite a bit, particularly after the run, so you would expect it to go up" on the pullback, said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in S&P 100 index .OEX options.
The volatility index, which is calculated off certain OEX options, was up 0.87, or 3.85 percent, at 23.50 at about 1100 CDT/1600 GMT.
At the same time, the OEX was down 1.07 at 912.80, the S&P 500 index .SPX was off 2.14 at 934.45 and September S&P 500 futures lost 0.90 at 941.40.
The Dow industrial average .DJI, which closed above 8,000 for the first time Wednesday, eased seven points to about 8,032.
Callahan said the market's softness drew some investors to buy August puts, action which he said had been largely absent in the market's run to record levels.
Among the August OEX puts, the August 910 was most active, with turnover of about 1,375 contracts. The August 870 traded about 1,090 and the August 900 traded roughly 530.
Most activity in OEX options was in the July series, which expires at the end of the week.
One OEX/SPX dealer in Chicago said he did not expect a volatile expiration.
"There have been call exercises all week but nothing major, nothing unexpected," he said.
Callahan added that trading in the expiring options was moderate.
"Nothing big, nothing unusual," Callahan said.
The OEX/SPX dealer said some volatility could emerge late Thursday.
"Tonight is going to be interesting, with Microsoft earnings coming out and exercises having to be in by 3:20 (1520 CDT/2020 GMT)," he said. "It could create quite a balancing act for people."
SPX options, which can only be exercised on expiration, expire today and investors have until 1520 CDT/2020 GMT to put in exercise orders.
If Microsoft's quarterly earnings, due out after the market closes today, are weaker than expected, they could knock the market for a loss Friday, the dealer said.
OEX options expire Friday.
"If Microsoft earnings are bad, they could really have an effect on things short-term," he said. "It would certainly affect the expiration a lot."
